title: 3694. Distinct Points Reachable After Substring Removal

examples.explanation: After removing a substring of length 1, s can be "UL", "LL" or "LU". Following these moves, the final coordinates will be (-1, 1), (-2, 0) and (-1, 1) respectively. There are two distinct points (-1, 1) and (-2, 0) so the answer is 2.
After removing a substring of length 4, s can only be the empty string. The final coordinates will be (0, 0). There is only one distinct point (0, 0) so the answer is 1.
After removing a substring of length 1, s becomes "U", which always ends at (0, 1), so there is only one distinct final coordinate.
